title: I Let My Neighbor Keep the Pressure Cooker Until the Quiet Portal Logged It

parts.text: I left the pressure cooker on Wren's stoop at 6:22 p.m. with the quiet-hours card I printed from the portal. Wren said steam was neighborly. I was forty-one, downstairs, standing in a hallway that made me look like I owned the hiss. The card said NO APPLIANCES AFTER SIX. Wren ran it anyway. I photographed the stoop, the hiss, and the portal receipt. Then I let the portal keep the timestamp. Wren laughed until compliance pinged the hiss. The cooker came back with a note. Wren portal-dates the loan now. A stoop is only a stoop until someone treats it like a clock.

social.video_title: The pressure cooker hissed after the quiet card — Part 1/1
social.description: Stoop, a six o'clock card, a portal ping. Compliance heard the hiss. Has a loan ever ignored the hours it borrowed?
